Philippines DOH · 90-minute course

Build your own POM

POM = Public Opinion Monitor. Taiwan CDC's system that reads television news for public-health signals. Today you build a mini version of it, then add your own idea.

Public Opinion MonitorColab+your own Claude

Taiwan CDC POM, 1 of 9

From frame to dashboard: three parts

AFilter by rulesevery frame, on the server
  • Capture a frame every 3 s
  • Crop the headline and ticker
  • Skip it if the picture did not change
  • Read the text (OCR)
  • Match the 328 keywords
  • Save the match with its screenshot
→
BAI patrolevery 10 minutes
  • Group repeat matches into one story
  • AI sorts the text into 9 topics
  • AI checks the screenshot: news or advertisement?
  • Write the tag back
→
CCheck by humanpeople have the last word
  • Look at the suspect results
  • Confirm or reject each one
  • Review repeating-advertisement candidates
  • Assign a category by hand
  • A person's tag is never overwritten

Taiwan CDC POM, 2 of 9

Phase A: every frame

A1Frame arrivesOne frame per channel every 3 s, from 10 live channels.
A2Crop the two regionsHeadline and ticker boxes, drawn by hand for each channel.
A3Did the picture change?Changed by 3% or more: read it. Unchanged: skip (but read at least every 60 s).
A4Read the text (OCR)An OCR model reads the strips. No speech recognition.
A5Keyword gateFalse forms are cut first, then the text is matched against 328 terms.
A6Save the matchA scrolling line is saved as one match, with a clean screenshot of the real broadcast frame.

Taiwan CDC POM, 3 of 9

Phase B: the AI patrol

B1Group into storiesEvery 10 minutes, new matches only. Repeat matches become one story.
B2Sort by topicAI checks each story and sorts it into one of 9 topics. Only public health goes on.
B3Check the screenshotAI looks at the whole frame: news or advertisement? Is the word really on screen?
B4Write backThe tag is written back to the story. A person's tag is never overwritten.

Taiwan CDC POM, 4 of 9

Phase C: people in charge

C1Suspect queueThe AI flags a match it doubts, for example the word is not meant literally. A flagged match still counts until a person decides: the word is fine, the word is false, or the story is not public health.
C2Repeating advertisementsA match that appears on many different days is a candidate advertisement. A person confirms it. Later matches are then compared by picture as well as by text.
C3Assign a categoryA person sets the topic of a whole story, for every channel and every repeat. It always wins: the AI and later rules never overwrite it.

Taiwan CDC POM, 5 of 9

The dashboard

  1. 1Word cloud: a bigger word means more screenshots.
  2. 2Filters: today, 7 days or any date; all, public health or other.
  3. 3Keyword chips by category: tick the ones you want.
  4. 4Trend line for the keywords you tick.
  5. 5Insights ticker: what is new compared with the previous window.
  6. 6Heatmap button: the next slides.

Taiwan CDC POM, 6 of 9

Click a word, see the frames

  • Click any word: you get every broadcast frame behind it.
  • Frames are grouped by story and by channel.
  • Each frame shows the channel, the time and the text that was read.
  • Nothing is taken from websites. Nothing is generated.

Taiwan CDC POM, 7 of 9

The rhythm of a keyword

  • One grid per keyword. Each row is a day (7 rows).
  • Each column is an hour of the day, from 0 to 23.
  • One cell is one hour of one day. A darker cell means more frames.
  • It shows when a topic is on air, not only how much.
  • Each keyword is shaded against its own range.

Taiwan CDC POM, 8 of 9

Watch it read, live

  • Pick a channel and see its live frame: one frame per channel every 3 seconds.
  • The headline box (blue) and ticker box (green) are drawn on the picture.
  • The text read from each box appears right below.
  • A layout check runs every 12 hours. A person fixes the boxes.

Back of the room

  • Next, you connect Claude to Colab. We explain Colab in a few slides. For now, just follow the steps.
  • Each team (A, B, C, D) chooses one person, the driver, to make the connection and run the notebook to the end. Choose the person with enough Claude quota.

Connect · 2.1

Open the Claude app and start a session

2.1Open the Claude app and start a session

Open the Claude app and sign in with your Claude account (skip this if you are already signed in). Start a new session. Choose a folder to work in (for example pom-work). If asked to trust it: Yes.

The Claude message box, ready in your work folder.

Connect · 2.2

Two small settings for Claude

ModelsPlan with Opus, work with Sonnet

In the model menu of the message box, choose Opus. When you ask for work, ask Claude to hand the work to Sonnet helpers (subagents). One message does it:

Message to paste (click the text to edit it)
Use Opus to plan this task. Then use Sonnet subagents to do the work, and tell me what each subagent did.
SafetyLock deleting and .env files

Paste this message. Claude edits your own settings so it cannot delete files and cannot read .env files. It shows you the result and asks before it saves.

Message to paste (click the text to edit it)
Please change my Claude user settings (the settings.json file in my .claude folder). Keep every setting I already have. Add two rules: 1) never delete anything: block rm, rmdir, unlink, shred, git rm, git clean and find -delete; 2) never read .env files: block reading .env and .env.* files in every folder. Show me the final file and ask me before you save it.

After this, Claude cannot delete files or folders, and cannot open .env files (the place where secret keys are often kept).

Connect · 2.3

Let Claude set up the rest

2.3Let Claude set up your tools

Paste the message. Approve what Claude asks. Click Yes if Windows asks. When it reports, start a new session in the same folder.

Message to paste (click the text to edit it)
I am on Windows. I want Claude to use Colab MCP (https://github.com/googlecolab/colab-mcp).
1. Check whether git and uv are installed. Install only what is missing (winget for git, Astral's official installer for uv).
2. Find the full path of uvx.exe and use that full path: a tool installed a minute ago may not be on PATH in this window yet.
3. Add a user-scope MCP server named colab-mcp that runs: <full path of uvx.exe> git+https://github.com/googlecolab/colab-mcp
4. Run `claude mcp get colab-mcp` and tell me the status.
If a step fails, do not stop: work out why and try another way until it works. Only ask me when you need me to click or approve something myself.
When it is done, tell me in a few lines what you did and the final status.
You should see

Claude installs only what is missing (git about 67 MB, uv about 16 MB), adds colab-mcp and says Connected. About 190 MB in total if nothing is installed yet (about 100 MB of it is Python and libraries). A few minutes.

Connect · what is Colab

What is Google Colab?

A notebook in your browserOne web page that mixes text and code. No install: you only need Chrome and your Google account.
Cells you run one by oneClick in a code cell and press Shift+Enter. The result appears right under it. Run from the top, down.
A computer in Google's cloudThe code does not run on your laptop. Press Connect: RAM and Disk show a Google computer is yours for now.
It forgetsLeave it idle or close the tab and the computer is taken back. Files on it disappear, so save or download what you want to keep.

Why Colab today: everyone gets the same clean computer, Tesseract installs in about a minute, and nothing touches your laptop. Later your own Claude will add cells to this same notebook.

Your notebook does all eight. Each step is a few lines of Python.

Your mini POM, 2 of 5

Find the two bands

  • Orange = the headline
  • Blue = the ticker, the scrolling line
  • Everything else is ignored: faces, trees, logos.

Real frame from clip_a. Every channel lays its screen out differently, so each channel needs its own boxes.

Your mini POM, 3 of 5

Read the text, skip repeats

OCR

Optical Character Recognition. A program looks at a picture of text and gives you the text back, as letters you can count and search.

Tesseract

A free, open-source OCR model, started at HP and developed by Google. It reads many languages: we use English and Filipino. A headline is read as a block of text, the ticker as one single line.

Your mini POM, 4 of 5

Keep only health words

  • A list of 180 words: English, plus a Filipino draft that still needs DOH review.
  • Text with no word from the list is dropped.
  • What is left is one table. Every new idea you build reads these rows.

    Demo together: stop the false WHO hits
    This is the first card, False triggers. We do it together before you start on your own.
    Message to paste (click the text to edit it)
    My Colab notebook is connected. First read /content/POM-Course/CONTEXT.md. Then do this as new cells at the end of the notebook; do not change my cells.
Some keyword hits in rows_sample.csv are not about health. For example, the word WHO in the sentence 'THOSE WHO ARE IN EMOTIONAL CRISIS' is a pronoun, not the World Health Organization.
Find rows like this, and add a way to leave them out. Show me the counts per keyword before and after, and list every row you removed so I can check each one.

    Hands-on · Bonus
    How the 30 minutes work, and how you share
    1. 1One direction per team (A to D). Pick together, about 3 minutes.

    Share: ask Claude for a one-page HTML
    Message to paste (click the text to edit it)
    Make a single-page HTML file that shows our result. Do not write paragraphs. Show a table with one row per example: the word, the line it appeared in, and a tick or a cross for whether it should count as health news. Put the ticks and crosses first so the page reads at a glance.
Use only real rows from rows_sample.csv or the new columns we made. Add one short line with the counts before and after. Put all styles inside the file so it opens by double-click. Tell me where the file is.
    Two minutes per team: what did you try? what did you find? what did Claude get wrong? what next? Show the page from the Colab tab or the saved file. If it does not open, show the table in your notebook.
    

    Hands-on · Demo
    Demo: an AI second opinion
    1 · The problem: same word, different context
    Dengue…BOHOL DECLARES DENGUE OUTBREAK✓
    Leptospirosis…EXPAND LEPTOSPIROSIS TREATMENT CAPACITY…✓
    WHO…THOSE WHO ARE IN CRISIS…✗
    Death…DEATH TOLL FROM RUSSIAN STRIKES✗
    Quarantine…AFFECTED BY THE COMMUNITY QUARANTINE; VISIT…✗
    ✓ health news   ✗ false trigger
    2 · What goes to the AI, step by step
    1
    Colab sends 8 hit rows at a time: only the text and the matched word."THOSE WHO ARE IN EMOTIONAL CRISIS" + WHO
    ↓
    2
    Google's AI reads them (Gemma). If it cannot decide, Colab also sends one frame picture to Flash-Lite.
    ↓
    3
    A short answer comes back for every row: health news or not, and is the word used in its own meaning?WHO → not its own meaning ✗
    Never leaves Colab: your key (it stays in Colab Secrets), the video, all other frames.
    3 · The main change
    231 → 221 hits
    10 hits removed: WHO 9 → 0, Death 1 → 0 (real run). A second opinion, not the truth.
    4 · The first prompt
    Message to paste (click the text to edit it)
    My notebook has a bonus cell at the end that asks an AI to double-check the keyword hits. I have added my key as the Colab secret GEMINI_API_KEY. Run that cell, then show me in a table which rows it kept and which it removed, with the reason it gave for each.
    

    Hands-on · Demo
    Get your own Gemini API key
    1Search
    Search Google for google AI studio and open the first result, or go straight to aistudio.google.com/apikey. Sign in with your Google account.
    2Open API Keys, then Create
    Click API Keys on the left (frame 1), then Create API key at the top right (frame 2). Black boxes hide the instructor's own keys.
    3Name it
    Keep the name and the default project. Click Create key.
    4Copy the key
    Click the copy button next to the key (frame 1), or Copy key (frame 2).
    5Save it in Colab Secrets
    In Colab: click the key icon on the left, then Add new secret. Name: GEMINI_API_KEY. Value: paste the key. Switch on Notebook access.
    The key is like a password. Never paste it into a chat, a cell or a slide. Before you leave today, delete it: open the key in AI Studio and click Delete key.
